title: Lead conversion experiments — angles & proof flows
body:
Purpose:
Quick reference doc for 3–4 homepage/landing hero variants and the supporting proof flows we will A/B test for the next two sprints. Goal: improve trial signups -> first API call conversion by 20% and reduce time-to-first-successful-call by 30%.

Audience:
Primary: engineering and ML teams evaluating inference providers. Secondary: platform/product buyer personas (infra, platform teams at mid-market to enterprise). They care about latency predictability, unit economics, deployment options, and operational observability.

Positioning thesis (short):
Redwood helps engineering teams ship LLM-powered features with predictable performance and controllable economics across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — so you can build fast without owning the infra.

Why this doc exists: small, testable hero variants + clear, machine-readable proof flows that map to metrics (trial->API call->dev success). Keep copy tight, engineer-friendly, and avoid generic platitudes. Emphasize operational primitives (SLOs, rollouts, caching) not just model names.

Hero angle A — "Developer velocity + predictable latency" (developer-first)
- Headline: "Build with models that behave in production"
- Subhead: "Fast, consistent inference across hosted, reserved, and private deployments — no last-minute surprises."
- 3 bullets (short):
  1) "Latency SLOs and regional routing for predictable responses"
  2) "SDKs + examples to go from notebook to endpoint in <1 hour"
  3) "Prefix and KV caching to lower tail latency at scale"
- CTA: "Start building — free credits"
- Primary proof: "99.95% of requests under 250ms in our benchmarks (seq len 512) — see perf sample"
- Tertiary microcopy: "Works with PyTorch/ONNX models; direct function calling; streaming responses."

Hero angle B — "Cost and throughput" (cost-conscious infra teams)
- Headline: "Predictably low per-token cost for real workloads"
- Subhead: "Autoscale reserved pools, intelligent batching, and quantization profiles that cut inference cost without sacrificing quality."
- 3 bullets:
  1) "Suggested batching/quantization per model by workload"
  2) "Dedicated pools + burst capacity for predictable throughput"
  3) "Cost breakdowns per token, route, and token type in the Console"
- CTA: "Estimate my cost"
- Primary proof: "Customer case: 48% cost reduction on chat workload via batching + KV cache"
- Microcopy: "Supports int8/int4 pipelines, per-route cost visibility, token-level billing."

Hero angle C — "Compliance and isolation" (enterprise/regulatory buyers)
- Headline: "Bring inference into your VPC or on-prem with full control"
- Subhead: "Private control plane, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit trails for regulated workloads."
- 3 bullets:
  1) "VPC-only deployments and private control plane options"
  2) "HSM/KMS integrations + audit logs for model and data access"
  3) "SLA-backed latency and uptime for Dedicated contracts"
- CTA: "Talk to sales — compliance brief"
- Primary proof: "SOC2 + enterprise pilot references available"
- Microcopy: "Air-gapped bundle available for highly regulated customers."

Hero angle D — "Quality + graceful degradation" (product managers focused on UX)
- Headline: "Keep your experience online, even under load"
- Subhead: "Automatic fallbacks, model variants, and region failover keep conversational and retrieval features resilient."
- 3 bullets:
  1) "Policy-based routing with automatic fallback to compatible model variants"
  2) "Eval-driven regression alerts tied to your prompt sets"
  3) "A/B rollouts and canary traffic split built-in"
- CTA: "See reliability playbook"
- Proof: "Integrated evals detected a 2% generation regression before a customer rollout."

Supporting page micro-templates (product detail sections):
- Hosting: Short paragraph that contrasts "Hosted API" (fast onboarding, pay-as-you-go) with "Dedicated" (predictable throughput, reserved GPU pools) and "Private" (VPC/HSM, audit logs). Keep to 2–3 sentences each; include quick bullets for SLOs, retention, and support tiers.
- How it works (3 steps):
  1) "Pick a model and deployment type — hosted/dedicated/private"
  2) "Configure routing, caching, and batching profiles (recommended presets)"
  3) "Deploy & measure — Console shows token-level cost, latency SLOs, and eval regressions"
- Quick proof modules to include on product pages: latency CDF chart (callout), cost-savings snapshot (callout), customer quote (short).

Competitive notes (short — quick scan for copy and claims to avoid):
- OpenAI: very broad model ecosystem and brand recognition; weakness: no reserved capacity SLA and limited on-prem/private options. Claim we can make: "Same developer ergonomics with deployment choices and SLA-backed capacity."
- Anthropic: safety-first and strong research credibility; weakness: enterprise deployment flexibility. Claim contrast: "Safety + production controls (rollouts + fallback) for product teams."
- Cloud vendors (GCP Vertex/AWS Bedrock/Azure): integrated infra but variance in price/perf and higher ops surface for multi-region inference routing. Claim: "Unified inference runtime across providers and deployment modes."
- Self-hosted runtimes (llama.cpp, private deployments): low nominal cost for small scale but heavy ops and lack of observability. Claim: "Save engineering cycles — run reliably without owning the entire inferencing stack."

Key messaging guardrails: avoid tactical model name brags (unless in model catalog); focus on operational outcomes: "predictability, unit economics, and control." Keep jargon accessible for product managers but include technical hooks for engineers (SLO, KV cache, autoscale).

A/B test plan (2-week sprint, sample):
- Variants: Developer-first (A), Cost-first (B), Compliance-first (C). Each variant maps to a dedicated landing microflow and sign-up CTA (free credits, cost estimator, contact).
- Audience split: 60% cold traffic (SEO + paid), 40% existing trial users and high-value accounts via targeted email.
- Metrics:
  * Primary: trial signups -> first API call conversion rate (target +20% over baseline)
  * Secondary: time-to-first-successful-call (target -30%), demo requests for compliance-tier
  * Tertiary: bounce rate on pricing & docs pages, NPS from trial cohort
- Sample success criteria: if variant lifts primary conversion by >12% with p<0.05 after N=2,000 unique visitors, roll variant to 50% traffic and re-evaluate.

Tracking & events (minimum):
- page_view.hero_variant = "developer|cost|compliance"
- clicked_cta = "free_credits|estimate_cost|contact_sales"
- sign_up.trial_created
- api_call.first_success
- eval.alert_triggered
- billing.estimate_requested

Microcopy snippets for CTAs and small copy tests (to A/B):
- "Start building — free credits" vs "Try the API free for 14 days"
- "Estimate my cost" vs "Get a cost estimate for my workload"
- "Talk to sales — compliance brief" vs "Request compliance pack"

Risks / unknowns:
- Our perf claims need up-to-date public benchmarks for the specific model families we surface — coordinate with applied-ml for a standard benchmark deck.
- Messaging that leans too compliance-heavy may reduce self-serve conversions; ensure the compliance CTA targets enterprise segments only.
- Cost-savings claims must be qualified (workload dependent). Add footnotes: typical chat/summary workload assumptions.

Next steps / owners (short):
- finalize hero copy options with design (Evan) — due 2026-03-07
- request perf snapshots from applied-ml (Marta) — due 2026-03-04
- wireframe microflows & tracking plan with analytics (Priya) — due 2026-03-06
- implement A/B experiment and QA (growth eng) — kickoff 2026-03-09

Notes to reviewers:
- Prefer lean wording; remove corporate filler. If a hero needs a shorter alt for mobile, aim for 6–7 words max.
- For proofs: include one inline data point and link to the benchmark artifact (Confluence).

Scratch ideas for later:
- "Playbook mode" — a single-page quick-start with recommended presets for chat, embeddings, and reranking workloads; include one-click 'apply preset' to console.
- Customer story micro-landing for '50% cost reduction' that walks through batching + caching + quantization steps (requires engineering validation).

End of doc.
